title: PwC 2026 AI Performance Study: 20% of Companies Capture 74% of AI Value
article_content:
LONDON, 13 April 2026 – A small group of companies is pulling sharply ahead in the race to generate real financial returns from artificial intelligence, according to PwC’s new AI Performance study. The global study interviewed 1,217 senior executives, primarily at large, publicly listed companies across 25 sectors, asking them about the revenue and efficiency gains they are seeing from AI today.

It finds that nearly three‑quarters (74%) of AI’s economic value is captured by just one‑fifth (20%) of organisations, revealing a stark and widening divide between a small group of AI leaders and the majority of businesses still stuck in pilot mode. The research shows that these top‑performing companies are not simply deploying more AI tools. Instead, they are using AI as a catalyst for growth and business reinvention, particularly by pursuing new revenue opportunities created as industries converge, while building strong foundations around data, governance and trust.

Key findings include:
- Growth vs. Productivity
- Decision Automation
- Trust and Governance

The study warns that without a shift in approach, the performance gap between AI leaders and laggards is likely to widen further as leaders scale proven use cases and automate decisions safely.

additional_sources.title: 'Minority' of firms turn AI efforts into measurable financial return
additional_sources.article_content: The Irish Examiner reports on the PwC study from an external business-news angle, emphasizing the economic concentration of AI benefits and the growing divide between companies scaling AI successfully and those stuck in experimentation. It highlights PwC’s conclusion that only a minority of firms are converting AI activity into measurable financial return and underscores the strategic implication that growth-oriented deployment matters more than pure cost-cutting. This source is useful because it reframes the study for a general business audience and strengthens the economic-angle writing with an independent interpretation of the widening performance gap rather than only repeating PwC’s own press-release language.

market_context_source.title: AI returns are concentrating among firms with data, scale and workflow control, executives say
market_context_source.article_content: The Wall Street Journal adds broader economic context by reporting that companies seeing meaningful AI returns tend to share structural advantages: proprietary data, large installed software bases, integration talent, and authority to redesign workflows rather than run isolated pilots. The article helps explain the concentration pattern in PwC’s findings by showing why value accrues unevenly across the economy. It also notes that many firms still face bottlenecks in data readiness, governance, and employee adoption, meaning the gap is not just about model access but about organizational capacity. That makes the PwC study part of a larger market story in which AI amplifies existing scale advantages and may deepen winner-take-most dynamics across sectors.
